_meta.project: instex Spectrograph Explorer presets -- round 8: LAMOST low-resolution spectrographs (Xinglong; id 'lamost')
_meta.rule: Every value carries src (key into sources), loc and a short verbatim quote from the saved document; DERIVED = arithmetic done here; INFERRED = a reading not stated; EFFECTIVE = fitted to published performance; MEASURED / SCHEMATIC for layout elements. Quotes machine-checked against pdftotext (layout, raw, flow) and tag-stripped HTML / ADS JSON.

parameters.name: telescope aperture D (nominal; the effective aperture varies with pointing)
parameters.value: 4.0 (nominal, the clear aperture that matches f/5 at 20 m); the effective aperture is 3.6-4.9 m: Table 2 of Cui et al. 2012 gives the equal-area diameter phi_0 of 4.881 m at dec -10 deg, 4.844 (0), 4.788 (10), 4.714 (20), 4.620 (30), 4.506 (40), 4.371 (50), 4.215 (60), 4.036 (70), 3.832 (80), 3.602 m (90 deg)
parameters.loc: table 'Main characteristics of LAMOST'; ADS abstract of Cui et al. 2012; PMC p. 1
parameters.note: HOW THE VARYING APERTURE IS HANDLED (updated): Cui et al. 2012 Sec. 2.6 says the entrance pupil is the projection of Ma, which changes with the pointing, 'the f-ratio is also not fixed'; Table 2 lists the equal-area diameter phi for each declination (the survey footprint, dec < 60 deg, spans phi = 4.2-4.9 m). The explorer needs one D: the preset keeps D = 4.0 m, the clear aperture (lamost.org) at which the stated focal ratio 5 holds for the 20 m focal length (Cui et al.: 'Its focal ratio is 5'). D enters only the virtual fiber angle core / (F_out D) and the Telescope box; the spectrograph does not change. Virtual core angle at phi = 4.88 m: 3.38 arcsec; at 4.0 m: 4.125; at 3.6 m: 4.58 (DERIVED, F_out = 4). A survey-weighted D (about 4.5 m at dec 40 deg) would change only the slit angle (3.67 arcsec); the 4.0 m choice keeps F = 4 and telF = 5 consistent.

parameters.derived: 20 / 4.881 = 4.10; 20 / 3.602 = 5.55. (First version: f/5 was DERIVED; now SOURCED.)

parameters.derived: 20 000 mm x (pi / 648 000) = 0.096963 mm/arcsec; 320 um / 96.963 um/arcsec = 3.300 arcsec (matches the published 3.3 arcsec exactly).

parameters.name: fiber slit (pseudo-slit): height, fiber pitch, curvature
parameters.value: 144 mm tall arc; 0.578 mm center-to-center; arc radius 691 +- 1 mm
parameters.derived: 250 x 0.578 = 144.5 mm (agrees with 144 mm). On the detector (x 250/800 = 0.3125): pitch 180.6 um = 15.05 px of 12 um (Song et al. 2017 measure 15-16 px: quote in 'fiber_spacing_check'); slit 45.0 mm = 3750 px of the 4096-px spatial axis. fgroups: the 250 fibers sit at a uniform pitch with no block gaps published (NOT FOUND whether v-groove blocks have gaps).

parameters.name: measured fiber spacing and profile width on the CCD
parameters.value: 15-16 pixels between adjacent fibers; profile FWHM about 7-8 pixels (cross-dispersion); monochromatic images 7-9 pixels FWHM

parameters.name: slit mask at the fiber output (survey mode)
parameters.value: 2/3 of the fiber width (2.2 arcsec of the 3.3 arcsec fiber) since 2011; the unmasked fiber gives the 'native' R ~ 1000
parameters.note: The mask narrows the slit across the dispersion; the fiber's spatial extent is unchanged. The explorer cannot give a different width across and along the dispersion except through traceW (as Via's 0.7 arcsec mask). The preset enters the masked slit as S3 x (2/3) of the virtual core angle (EFFECTIVE; see the fit below).

parameters.name: fiber output focal ratio (collimator input)
parameters.loc: Zhu et al. 2000 abstract; Hou et al. 2010 abstract
parameters.note: ('bema' is the abstract's own typo.) The fiber input ratio is the telescope's (20 m / D_eff = f/4.1-f/5.6); the f/4 collimator is the explorer's F. Explorer convention (virtual, as APOGEE, BOSS, DESI): slit angle = core / (F_out D) = 0.320 mm / (4 x 4000 mm) = 4.125 arcsec, equal-line-width slit S3 x 4.125 = 3.57 arcsec; telescope box telF = 5, fibAp = 3.3 arcsec (on-sky).

parameters.name: collimator type
parameters.value: Schmidt collimator: spherical mirror with a Schmidt correction, f/4
parameters.note: Explorer: col 'mirror'. Fig. 30(b) draws the collimator as one concave mirror; no Schmidt corrector is drawn in front of it, and Cui et al. do not describe one. Huang et al. 2020's 'two Schmidt correcting mirrors' is not supported by Cui et al. (see Conflicts).

parameters.name: collimator focal length and beam diameter
parameters.value: f_col = 800 mm; beam 200 mm (f/4)
parameters.derived: 800 / 200 = 4.0, f/4. MEASURED check on Fig. 30(b) (img 1654 x 909 px, see Layout): slit-to-collimator 515 px, returning beam 130 px wide: 515 / 130 = 3.96, so the drawing is to scale with f = 800 mm, 1.553 mm/px.

parameters.name: collimator on-axis or off-axis (DEPLOY GATE)
parameters.value: ON-AXIS: the fiber slit stands in the middle of the returning collimated beam, on the collimator's axis (MEASURED from Cui et al. 2012 Fig. 30(b), a to-scale layout); no tilt or off-axis distance is published or drawn; no sentence states it
parameters.note: UPGRADED from INFERRED. The paper contains no sentence about the slit standing in the returning beam or about a central obscuration (searched: 'obscur', 'slit', 'Schmidt'). Fig. 30(b), however, draws it: the SLIT is a thin vertical bar on the horizontal axis 515 px (= 800 mm = f_col, MEASURED) in front of the collimator mirror; the rays leave it toward the mirror as an f/4 cone, and the collimated beam (130 px = 200 mm) returns leftward along the same axis, straddling the bar, with arrows in both directions on one axis. The slit bar (94 px = 146 mm tall, agreeing with the sourced 144 mm) is seen edge-on, so it cuts a thin strip out of the beam; its width (the obscuration) is NOT FOUND. A Schmidt collimator is a spherical mirror with the focal surface on its axis, so this is the on-axis geometry. The remaining uncertainty is that the verdict still comes from a drawing, not a sentence.

parameters.name: dichroic beam splitter (split in the collimated beam)
parameters.value: blue reflected, red transmitted; angle of incidence about 23 deg (MEASURED from Fig. 30(b), +-4 deg); the dichroic stands in the 200 mm collimated beam about 1230 mm from the collimator; cut ~5800 A (INFERRED) and width NOT FOUND
parameters.derived: Cui et al. do not give the cut wavelength, the transition width or the angle ('diachronic' is their spelling). INFERRED cut = 5800 A (middle of the stated 570-590 nm overlap). Fig. 30(b) MEASURED (to scale, 1.553 mm/px): the dichroic is a tilted slab centered 792 px = 1230 mm from the collimator (275 px = 427 mm past the slit); the slab's long axis stands 26 deg from the perpendicular to the beam (AOI 26 deg); the reflected blue rays leave 41 deg above the rightward horizontal, a turn of 139 deg, i.e. AOI 20.5 deg. The two readings disagree by 5 deg; adopted AOI = 23 +- 4 deg. The blue beam is turned clockwise (as drawn) by 139 deg back toward the collimator side and travels 355 px = 551 mm to the blue grating. Width: NOT FOUND (placeholder 500 A, not a LAMOST number).

parameters.name: red-channel VPH grating (low-resolution mode), transmission
parameters.value: design 540 /mm; measured 548 /mm (units 2-16; unit 1: 547); AOI 8.63 deg, AOD 14.46 deg external; center wavelength 740 nm; first order; 220 x 220 x 20 mm
parameters.derived: DERIVED check of Table 1 with the grating equation sin(AOI) + sin(AOD) = G lambda: red 540 /mm, 740.46 nm: sin 8.63 + sin 14.46 = 0.1500 + 0.2497 = 0.3998 = 540 x 740.46e-6 = 0.3998 (exact). Camera-collimator angle AOI + AOD = 23.09 deg (red) and 22.17 deg (blue). In the explorer: gType 'trans', tAlpha = 8.63 (external AOI, as DESI), lamC = 7404.6 A (design center, as DESI uses the grating-equation center).
parameters.note: The measured densities (548 red, 813 blue) are 1.5% above the design; the dispersion fits better with them (camera 252 vs 256 mm below). The preset uses the measured values. Table 1's red-grating blaze/Bragg numbers conflict with the text (see Conflicts).

parameters.name: blue-channel VPH grating (low-resolution mode), transmission
parameters.value: design 800 /mm; measured 813 /mm (units 2-16; unit 1: 811); AOI 8.17 deg, AOD 14 deg external; center wavelength 480.38 nm (Cui Table 6; Xiong's '2.033' is a misprint); range 365-590 nm; first order; 220 x 220 x 20 mm; efficiency about 80%
parameters.derived: DERIVED check: sin 8.17 + sin 14.0 = 0.3840 = 800 x 480.0e-6 (480.38 nm in Cui Table 6: 0.3843, 0.1% apart). Xiong's Table 1 misprint '2.033' is resolved by Cui et al. Table 6 (480.38). With the measured 813 /mm and the same angles the grating-equation center would be 472 nm (red: 548 /mm gives 729 nm); the preset keeps the design centers (lamC 4804 and 7405 A) so that the chip covers the design bands.

parameters.name: R = 5000 gratings (one unit each, 2011 test set)
parameters.note: Cui Table 5: medium-resolution mode, blue 510-540 nm and red 830-890 nm, R = 5000 (full slit), 7500 (2/3), 10 000 (1/2), 20 000 (1/4). These are the 2011 gratings (Table 6: 1680 and 2750 /mm, AOI 43.9, AOD 49.1, one set installed). The 2017 MRS gratings (coverage 4950-5350 and 6300-6800 A, DR12) are a different set; their line densities and angles are NOT FOUND.

parameters.name: camera type, focal length, focal ratio
parameters.value: two articulating Schmidt cameras, f/1.3 (SOURCED, Cui et al. 2012): f_cam = 1.3 x 200 mm = 260 mm (DERIVED, 255-265 mm for f/1.25-1.35 rounding); adopted 250 mm (EFFECTIVE, from the published dispersions; within the f/1.3 rounding); a field lens at the dewar window
parameters.derived: UPGRADED: the camera ratio is now SOURCED (f/1.3). f_cam = 1.3 x 200 = 260 mm (the paper rounds to 2 figures: 250 mm gives f/1.25, which rounds to 1.3). The dispersions give f_cam = cos(beta) / (G x dlam/dx): red cos 14.46 / (548 /mm x 7.0e-6) = 252.4 mm (540 /mm: 256.2); blue cos 14.0 / (813 x 4.75e-6) = 251.3 mm (800: 255.3); the fiber pitch (15-16 px) gives 250-266 mm; the 7-9 px image width is consistent with 250 mm. The explorer with 260 mm would give dispersion 0.814 and 0.550 A/px (-3.1% and -3.5% against 0.84 and 0.57); with 250 mm +0.8% and +0.3%. Adopted 250 mm (EFFECTIVE, inside the published f/1.3 rounding); 260 mm is the nominal alternative.
parameters.note: Explorer: cam 'mirror' (a catadioptric camera with an internal focus: the Schmidt corrector, a spherical mirror and the detector with its dewar inside the beam, as Hectospec).

parameters.name: detector format and pixel
parameters.value: 4096 x 4136 active pixels (4096 along the slit, 2 x 2068 = 4136 along the dispersion), 12 um square, e2v (EEV) CCD203-82, 49.2 mm x 49.2 mm image area; two per spectrograph (blue and red), 32 in all; read through two outputs
parameters.derived: Orientation: SO17 says the dispersion runs along the vertical direction of the 4096 x 4136 image, so the explorer's Nx (dispersion) = 4136 and Ny = 4096. 4136 x 12 um = 49.6 mm. The early design (Zhu et al. 2000) had 2048 x 2048 pixels; the CCD page notes the chip 'may be operated efficiently as a 2048 x 2068 24 um-pixel imager' with 2 x 2 binning.

parameters.name: dispersion

parameters.derived: Model check (explorer physics.js, D 4.0, F 4, W 200, fcam 250, 548 /mm, AOI 8.63 deg, lamC 7404.6 A): 0.847 A/px (+0.8%); blue 813 /mm, AOI 8.17, lamC 4800 A: 0.572 A/px (+0.3%).

parameters.value: Cui et al. Table 4 (the designers' values): full slit 1000, 1/2 slit 2000, 2/3 slit 1500, 1/4 slit 4000, for both arms; the survey runs the 2/3 slit: R = 1500 (Cui et al. 2012) versus R = 1800 quoted by the data-release headers, Huang et al. and Zhao et al.
parameters.tag: SOURCED (nominal; not stated whether arc-line measured)
parameters.derived: Geometric check, no mask: slit image 320 um x 250/800 = 100 um; at 70 A/mm (red) 7.0 A = R 1058 at 7405 A; blue 100 um x 47.5 A/mm = 4.75 A = R 1010 at 4800 A (both ~1000). Unmasked (S3 x 4.125 arcsec = 3.57 arcsec): 1185 and 1138.

parameters.name: medium-resolution survey mode (MRS)
parameters.value: R ~ 7500 (2/3 slit), since the 2017 upgrade; blue 4950-5350 A (R 7500 at 5163 A), red 6300-6800 A (R 7500 at 6593 A); survey began September 2018
parameters.note: MRS is NOT well documented for the explorer: the grating line densities, angles, camera angles and focal lengths of the 2017 mode are NOT FOUND (Hou et al. 2018 is SPIE, not retrievable). Fig. 4 shows the MRS channels as the same collimator and dichroic with the cameras moved to other positions ('changing cameras to different positions', LSPEC). A preset would need those numbers; not recommended yet.

parameters.name: survey spectrum counts
parameters.value: LRS: 12,602,390 spectra in DR12 v1.0 (12,231,890 stellar, 281,059 galaxy, 89,441 quasar); MRS: 3,365,641 coadded and 12,110,344 single-exposure spectra; about 17 million spectra released by the end of 2021

parameters.name: (telescope context)
parameters.value: Schmidt-corrector telescope: Mb 6.67 m x 6.05 m (37 segments), Ma 5.72 m x 4.40 m (24 segments)

parameters.name: stability requirement
parameters.value: image movement < 0.6 um/h (0.05 pixel/h); radial velocity 4 km/s over the 5 deg FOV in 2 h

parameters.name: layout distances (Fig. 30(b)) and element order
parameters.value: collimator -> slit 800 mm (on-axis, MEASURED = f_col); collimator -> dichroic 1230 mm; dichroic -> red grating 520 mm (red path from the collimator 1750 mm); dichroic -> blue grating 551 mm (blue path 1781 mm); grating -> Schmidt corrector 185 mm (both arms); camera axis bends 22-23 deg after the grating
parameters.derived: Method: the embedded image (1654 x 909 px) was extracted with pdfimages and read on a pixel grid. Scale from f = 800 mm (SOURCED) = slit-to-collimator 515 px, i.e. 1.553 mm/px; check: the returning beam is 130 px = 202 mm (SOURCED 200 mm) and the slit bar 94 px = 146 mm (SOURCED 144 mm), so the figure is to scale. Positions in px (x along the beam axis, mirror vertex at x = 1612): slit 1095, dichroic center 820, red VPHG ~485, a thin plate at x = 585 between the dichroic and the red grating (purpose NOT FOUND), red Schmidt corrector slab ~(370, 695), red camera mirror at the left edge. Distances: 1612-1095 = 517 px = 803 mm; 1612-820 = 792 px = 1230 mm; 820-485 = 335 px = 520 mm; total 1127 px = 1750 mm; blue: (820,724) to the blue VPHG (1100,505) = 355 px = 551 mm, total 1781 mm; grating to corrector 119 px = 185 mm. Uncertainty +-5% on the beam-axis distances (edge reading of the drawn slabs), +-15% on the camera distances. Camera axis bend: red 22 deg (grating to mirror center, 385 px by 155 px), blue 21 deg, against 23.09 and 22.17 deg from Cui Table 6 (AOI + AOD, DERIVED).
